extracted.intended_audience: NIH-style grant applicants and institutional grants administrators preparing Facilities & Other Resources, equipment, biosketches, and budget sections (PA-16-191 example)
extracted.subtask_description: Assembling the Facilities & Other Resources, Major Equipment, Senior/Key Person profiles, biosketches, and Research & Related budget forms for an NIH-style grant application (example: PA-16-191). Includes documenting institutional resources, core facilities, equipment, collaborations, personnel effort, and budget line items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and Resources Overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview: IUSM was established in 1903... The main medical center campus... consists of 18 buildings and four hospitals... research laboratory and support space encompasses approximately 619,000 net assignable square feet. An additional 41,000 net assignable square feet of IUSM-leased lab space is located off campus at partner health institutions. The academic faculty comprises of ~2,000 full-time faculty across more than 60 clinical departments and 29 research institutes. For FY2014-15, IUSM received approximately $302 million in sponsored programs funding, $111 million of which came from the NIH. IUSM currently hosts 12 research centers or program projects supported by PHS/NIH or other federal funds, and at least 20 supported by non-federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe institutional scale and environment: campus/hospitals, lab/net assignable square footage, numbers of faculty, recent sponsored funding (especially NIH), federally-supported centers and training programs. Provide concrete counts and figures to demonstrate institutional capacity and research environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory space and local equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: I have 500 square feet independent laboratory space (R4 Room 451B) adjacent to the laboratory of Dr. Chandy John... My laboratory is equipped with: a -80°C freezer, a -20°C freezer/refrigerator, a refrigerated Eppendorf 5430R centrifuge, an Eppendorf 5424 centrifuge, a microwave, water baths, a heat block, Mettler-Toledo scale, vortexes, a Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer, a mini-incubator, a BioTek 96-well plate washer with magnetic adapter, a Bio-Rad C1000 Touch thermal cycler, and an upright and inverted phase microscope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the lab footprint, which instruments are located in the PI’s lab versus shared, and note shared service arrangements (e.g., shared biosafety cabinets, incubators). Be specific about equipment model/types and storage (e.g., -80°C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to flow cytometry and cell-sorting core facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: As a member of the Wells Center, I will have unlimited access to a BD FACSCanto II capable of 6-color flow cytometer for routine FACS experiments. Walther Hall houses the flow cytometry core facility, which contains two BD FACSCalibur (three and four colors) and two BD LSRII (nine and 10 colors) flow cytometers as well as BD FACSAria (10 colors), BD SORP Aria (15 colors), and iCyt Reflection (nine colors) cell sorters. Both the FACSAria and SORP Aria are BSL2+. In addition, IUSM recently acquired a CyTOF2 Mass cytometer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document core facilities accessible to the project, list instruments (including color/capacity and BSL level), and core services (multi-parameter immunofluorescence, cell sorting, single cell sorting, cell cycle analysis, kinetic analysis). Specify if instruments are shared and any special capabilities (e.g., CyTOF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical sites and disclosure of clinical effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical sites: IUSM and its affiliated hospitals are located on or near the IUPUI campus... I will devote no more than 20% effort to clinical responsibilities. I will maintain a one half-day Infectious Diseases clinic every other week... I will also provide 6 weeks of clinical service per year as the Infectious Diseases consult attending at Methodist, University, or Roudebush Hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State affiliated clinical sites and clearly disclose percent effort devoted to clinical responsibilities and clinical schedules that may affect research time. Quantify clinical service commitments (e.g., clinic half-day every other week; number of weeks/year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office, computing, software and secure data storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Offices: I have a fully furnished office within the Wells Center ... personal phone, computer, and printer... Computers: I will be using a 15-inch MacBook Pro ... and a MacPro ... Appropriate software will be installed... I maintain an NIH/NIAID MacBook Pro laptop through my Special Volunteer status at the NIH, in conjunction with my co-mentor Dr. Crompton, allowing access to an encrypted NIH server for collaborative work. The computers at IUSM are connected via Ethernet or secured Wi-Fi ... Research data is backed up from the servers to on-site disk backup devices using 256-bit AES encryption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe office location, primary computing hardware, key software packages (e.g., R, SAS, FlowJo), network access, and data backup/encryption procedures. Mention any secure/external server access (e.g., NIH server) relevant to collaborative data sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational biology, bioinformatics, and HPC resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The IUSM Center for Computational Biology and Bioinformatics (CCBB) can provide additional computational support... Statistical packages include R, SAS, S-PLUS, SigmaPlot, nQuery Advisor, DBMScopy, Solas, LogXact, StatXact, and SPSS. The center also maintains a network of UNIX systems... For statistical analysis requiring high-performance parallel computing, I will have access to the IU supercomputers, which include IU's Big Red II (one petaflops), Big Red (40.96 teraflops), Quarry cluster (26.22 teraflops), and Mason large-memory (8TB) cluster (3.81 teraflops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List bioinformatics support, available statistical software, UNIX/cluster resources, and access to institutional high-performance computing (give machine names and rough capacities). Note availability of specialist staff for mapping/visualization/NGS support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative, grants management and career-development support
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative support: The Division of Infectious Diseases provides administrative support for this project. The Department of Medicine provides support for website design and maintenance, grants management expertise, and appropriate laboratory and office space. In addition, the Department has a dedicated and engaged Vice Chair of Research Dr. Samir Gupta who provides career development support for junior faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe administrative units that will support the project (grants management, website, space), and name institutional individuals or offices that provide career development or mentorship. Highlight services that reduce administrative burden on the PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for Early Stage Investigators (institutional programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources for Early Stage Investigators: IUSM is committed to promoting the development and advancement of early stage investigators and offers the following resources: A. The Indiana Clinical and Translational Sciences Institutes (CTSI) offers Young Investigator Awards... B. The Independent Investigator Incubator (I3)... C. The Leadership in Academic Medicine Program (LAMP)... D. The Indiana-CTSI Project Development Teams...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant is an early stage investigator, document available institutional programs (pilot funding, mentoring, professional grant writers, biostatistics, IRB/regulatory support, project development teams) that support career development and the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborating sites and external laboratory support
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborating sites: Human samples will be obtained from the NIH in collaboration with Dr. Peter Crompton at NIAID and with the support of Dr. Boubacar Traore in the MRTC in Mali. The laboratory of Dr. Philip L. Felgner within the Institute for Immunology, UC Irvine will support protein array studies. The Laboratory of Multiscale Regenerative Technologies, directed by Dr. Sangeeta Bhatia, will support studies involving the microscale human liver platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify external collaborators, describe the specific support they provide (sample sources, assays, platforms), and specify roles and responsibilities for collaborative tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major equipment availability and shared core instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Equipment: Dr. Tran’s laboratory is equipped with four BSL2 biosafety cabinets shared with two other investigators at the Wells Center. His laboratory will also have the following: a -80°C freezer, a -20°C freezer/refrigerator, a refrigerated Eppendorf 5430R centrifuge... Dr. Tran will share the following equipment with Dr. John: Bio-Rad MAGPIX multiplex reader, ELISA microplate reader, Bio-Rad plate washer, LabChip GX Touch HT microfluidic device, Bio-Rad Tetrad Thermal Cycler, Applied Biosystems QuantStudio 6 Flex Real-Time PCR System with 96- and 384-well blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List major pieces of equipment available to the project (including shared items), indicate which are shared vs. dedicated, and identify core labs that house additional instruments and services.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach a complete NIH-format biosketch for each Senior/Key person and include current & pending support documents. Use the required file names and mime types specified by the forms and include all senior personnel listed on the profile pages.
